tasks.short: Write flight times, altitudes and fuel consumption in flight records.

steps.what: Gather actual flight times, altitude information and fuel readings for the flown sector
Calculate flight durations and fuel consumption from verified source values
Write specified information in flight records, including times, altitudes and fuel consumption
Verify the complete flight record against actual sector conditions and approve its revision
Commit the approved flight record to the operator's electronic records system

tasks.design: Configure native source-value import and fixed calculation fields in the electronic-flight-record category of {OTHER}. The pilot checks the complete sector record against actual operations before a version-bound commit; no model fills missing flight facts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper source values, repeated calculations and record transcription duplicate sector information.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported aircraft exports and native record fields can reuse actual values and fixed formulas.
tasks.still_hard: Incorrect sector matching, units or time definitions can produce convincing but false records.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve anomalies from actual flight knowledge and attest to an accurate record.
tasks.altitude: Less record transcription; pilot attestation remains unchanged.

reach.role: airline pilot, copilot or flight engineer

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supported aircraft exports and electronic flight-record fields can reduce repeated entry, provided source identity, units and operator definitions are checked.

assumptions: Boundary begins after a flown sector and ends with its operator record; it does not include controlling the aircraft. Shares are provisional for a manual-recording workflow; aircraft logging runtime is excluded.

Aircraft exports, where available, supply registration, sector timestamps, altitude events, fuel values and units. s1 verifies sector identity and manually captures unavailable values and operational exceptions in retained time. No sensor availability or clean fuel-consumption field is assumed universally.

Operator supplies event definitions, duration formula, fuel-unit conversion and handling of refuelling. s2 never substitutes planned values for actuals; missing inputs block the draft until pilot correction. s3 uses the same verified source snapshot.

Test native import and record configuration first. s4 reviews all final fields, including sources and any correction, before s5. Changes invalidate approval; staff-linked records require appropriate access and applicable consultation.
research_questions: Can each imported record field be traced to the correct actual sector and unit without extra pilot correction?

already_counted.description: Verify and approve final flight record

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings, formula validation and offline synchronization checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete flight-record revision, actual sector and source snapshot approved in s4; changed fields require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 15 gathering, 20 calculation, 30 transcription and five commit hours less three upkeep. Low assumes native import and calculations already operate, leaving commitment only. Pilot verification remains full time; no in-flight labour saving is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate flight activities and brief crew on procedures.

steps.what: Retrieve the current flight details, ground arrangements and applicable test procedures
Coordinate flight activities with ground crews and resolve readiness issues
Coordinate with air traffic control and confirm flight instructions through required readback
Inform crew members of flight and test procedures and confirm understanding

tasks.design: Configure a native flight-specific reference view in the flight-operations category of {OTHER}. Reduce repeated document navigation while retaining all ground coordination, air-traffic communication and crew briefing time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current details and applicable procedure revisions may sit across several views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native flight-linked document views can present the relevant existing sources together.
tasks.still_hard: Readiness and instructions can change during the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain shared situational understanding and resolve ambiguity immediately.
tasks.altitude: Less reference navigation; operational communication and decision rights are unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: flight-linked reference views can reduce document navigation, but cannot replace live coordination or required confirmation of instructions.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference retrieval and live flight coordination. Formal flight-plan filing and post-flight record commitment are separate tasks, not folded into a conversation. Shares are provisional.

Existing operations producers supply flight ID, aircraft, route, time and procedure revision links. s1 checks identity and currency, manually retrieves missing sources and retains all substantive reading.
{OTHER} includes flight-operations reference tools and aviation radio. No model interprets or transmits clearances; the design performs read-only reference support and no automated send or commit.
Test native flight packs and bookmarks first. No saving is assigned to live communication, readback or ground-crew labour. Existing consolidated views earn no new saving.
research_questions: Can native reference views reduce navigation while preserving currency checks and full source visibility?

incremental.description: Maintain reference links and revision checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes eight repeated-reference-navigation hours less one upkeep. Low assumes a consolidated native flight pack already exists, leaving upkeep only. All live coordination and briefing remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform minor aircraft maintenance or arrange major maintenance.

steps.what: Assess the aircraft defect and confirm the pilot's permitted maintenance scope
Perform permitted minor aircraft maintenance and check the completed work
Draft the aircraft technical-log entry for the defect and any permitted work
Approve the exact technical-log entry and its stated maintenance limitations
Commit the approved defect and maintenance entry to the aircraft technical log
Discuss major maintenance needs, access and timing with the authorized maintenance provider
Draft the maintenance request with the actual defect and proposed arrangements
Approve the final major maintenance request and provider destination
Send the approved major maintenance request to the authorized provider

tasks.design: Use native prefilling and entry masks in the electronic-technical-log category of {OTHER}. Keep maintenance scope, physical work and provider coordination human; separately gate the final log commit and the completed external maintenance request.
tasks.previous_blocker: Aircraft identity and recurring log fields are re-entered, and requests require separate delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Native technical-log fields and approved-message routing can reuse verified information.
tasks.still_hard: A pilot's permission to perform a task is limited, and a log entry is not an airworthiness release.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize the limit of permitted work and ensure qualified maintenance handles the remainder.
tasks.altitude: Less log repetition; maintenance competence and release authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: AVIATAR Technical Logbook supports prefilled text, input masks, offline sync and maintenance-system links; this supports log mechanics rather than physical maintenance.

assumptions: This is a provisional mixed-case allocation across minor-work and major-arrangement cases, not a requirement that every defect follows both branches. Minor-only cases stop after s5; major-only cases have no physical repair in s2 and record the defect before s6. Shares must be remeasured for the actual mix.

Aircraft records supply registration, type and log context. s1 checks instructions and permission. s2's physical work and checks remain unchanged; s3 manually captures actual defect, action, time and limitations while native fields reuse identity. No completion or serviceability status is inferred.

s6 retains all provider discussion. s7 manually writes the actual request, including aircraft, defect reference, location, proposed time and authorized scope. It exists before s8 approval; request delivery does not authorize extra work or cost beyond existing authority.

Test native log masks and routing first. Changed log content voids s5 approval; changed request or provider voids s9 approval. External maintenance execution and qualified release effort are outside this pilot's saving and never automated by this design.
research_questions: Does native prefilling reduce entry while keeping defect and completed-work statements distinct?

already_counted.description: Verify final log entry and limitations

incremental.description: Maintain identity mappings and technical-log synchronization checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact technical-log revision, actual defect and permitted-work statements approved in s4; edits require renewed approval
Complete maintenance request, actual arrangements and provider address approved in s8; changes void send approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes six recurring-log-field, five commit and five request-dispatch hours less two upkeep. Low assumes current native log and dispatch already provide these functions. Physical maintenance, decisions and provider discussion remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review crew identities, assigned duties and current operational procedures
Decide crew responsibilities and resolve readiness or workload concerns
Brief other crew members on responsibilities and confirm their understanding
Supervise other crew members and intervene when coordination or safety deteriorates
Debrief crew members on coordination and immediate improvements

tasks.design: Configure a native crew-and-procedure reference view in the flight-operations category of {OTHER}. Retain all duty decisions, crew communication, supervision and debriefing; reduce repeated roster and document navigation only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Roster and current procedure references may require separate lookups before supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native flight-linked views can place existing references together.
tasks.still_hard: Workload and coordination can change rapidly and are not captured by roster status.
tasks.human_edge: Notice deteriorating performance and invite crew members to raise concerns.
tasks.altitude: A small reference benefit; supervisory responsibility stays with the pilot.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: flight-linked crew and procedure views can reduce reference navigation without supervising people or deciding fitness for duty.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference review, responsibility decisions, oral briefing, live supervision and oral debrief. No routine written performance assessment or roster amendment is assumed; if required, it must be separately captured, reviewed and committed. Shares are provisional.
Operations supplies existing crew roster, flight ID, roles and procedure revisions. s1 checks identity and missing information manually. No new crew scoring or observation dataset is collected.
The reduced part of s1 is repeated navigation only; assessing readiness in s2 and supervising in s4 retain full time. Test native views first. Crew members' own labour receives no saving.

This task's reference review is distinct from ground and air-traffic coordination in the other task; shared roster lookup must be assigned once in any team roll-up. No automated communication or record commitment is proposed.
research_questions: Is there distinct repeated reference lookup after existing crew briefing preparation?

incremental.description: Maintain crew reference links and access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five distinct reference-navigation hours less one upkeep. Low assumes native views already exist or overlap is owned by another task, leaving upkeep only. All crew decisions and interactions remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native flight and technical records around unchanged operational and safety responsibilities.
role.ambitious_version: Reduce repeated record handling while preserving pilot, crew and maintenance decision rights.
